relevance_note: The paper reports two adult siblings with GAMT deficiency carrying a homozygous variant: "Exome sequencing identified a homozygous nonsense variant in GAMT in both affected siblings", plus a table of 21 previously published adult cases.
method_note: Built with a Python script in the scratch directory; every value was chosen by reading the paper and the script only located table cells and checked spans. Table 1 has patients as columns: data column 1 = 'Individual V-1', columns 2 and 3 = 'Individual V-3' (column 3 = re-examination 2 years later at age 25); V-3 spans run through column 2 or 3. Table 2 literature rows 1-21 are labelled 'Table 2 #<n>' from the bare 'No.' column (superscript sibling/twin markers a,b,c,d,t dropped from the label); rows 22-23 are V-1 and V-3. Table 2 '+' cells were read as present (column headers ID/GDD, E, Behavioral abn); the legend does not define '−', so '−' cells were left not reported; 'na/nr' not reported. Table 2 age: per legend, plain age = age at diagnosis; age* = age at publication (recorded as age at last evaluation). For V-1/V-3 the Table 2 ages (25, 23) were recorded as age at diagnosis per the legend, although they match the examination ages in Table 1. Row 9 speech cell joins two source descriptions with ' / ' (one person per row, not a stacked multi-patient cell), so both were assigned to that person. Row 14 variant column says 'not reported'; no variant row was created because the paper does not tie a specific GAMT variant to that person. Literature zygosity is not stated per row, so left not reported (row 1 lists two variants). Relatives: the unaffected parents (sex not given, labelled 'parent of V-1'/'parent of V-1 2') and unaffected sister V-4 were Sanger-tested; the paper states segregation in an autosomal recessive mode but not each relative's genotype, so no variant rows and inheritance for V-1/V-3 left not reported. The other untested 'healthy' sibling gets no row. 'Peripheral neuropathy: Probably present' (Table 1) and 'Arthritis: Not tested / Not clinically confirmed' are hedged and not recorded as features. Birth facts ('The children were born at full term ... normal birth weight, height and head circumference') recorded as excluded for V-1 and V-3 as a group statement. Checklist 'absent or limited speech' was marked observed for 'Speech/language delay' entries; 'developmental regression' observed for V-1 (motor regression from 5 y), V-3 (progressive motor decline), Table 2 #1 (motor regression ~30 yo) and #9 (lost speech). Hyper−/dystonia mapped to dystonia. n_patients_reported left null: the paper reports 2 own cases plus 21 literature cases but states no single total. A previously published 30-month-old boy carrying the same variant (ref [25]) is included. No internal contradictions found.
